label: early original-phase step: d/r/p/i/k/s-type token after early q/a/l/1/n
explanation: Fires mainly during the original phase (83% of mass), peaking at t=2-4 and never at t=0. It is almost silent on the delimiter and weak in the copy phase. It looks like a graded additive response: some current tokens push it up (d, r, p, i, k, s, then t, 2, b, h, w) and so do some recent or earlier tokens (q strongest, then a, l, 1, n, c, x, v), especially at prev/prev2 positions and as first_tok. The largest activations are on a d/p/r/s/t token right after a q (e.g. a q q [p] ...). No boolean predicate captures this well. The best one (early original step, an enhancing token seen before, current token in the enhancing set) gets dev F1 0.40, precision 0.43, mass recall 0.50. Many false positives use the same token sets, and many misses fall outside them. Magnitude grows with q directly preceding (prev/prev2) and with position t=2-4. Unchecked: any finer magnitude ordering.
